name: Celestial Blue
lede: Celestial blue was a name in the paint shop before it was a color on a chart: a pale, reduced tint of Prussian blue, also used in French for cerulean.

sections.title: A pale Prussian blue
sections.body: In the Pigment Compendium, celestial blue is Prussian blue struck onto a base such as baryte (barium sulfate), as a pale tint of 5 to 10 percent [1]. It is similar to Brunswick blue and, by the account of Heaton (1928), the same as daylight blue [1]. A Victorian manual quoted there, Davidson (1880), gives the recipe: alumina precipitated from alum, mixed with baryta, iron sulfate, yellow prussiate of potash and some bichromate [2]. Dried, it is Brunswick or celestial blue; without the baryta, and kept wet, it is *damp blue* [2]. [[prussian-blue]] was the colorant, and the base made it pale and cheap.

sections.title: A second meaning
sections.body: The same words name a different paint in French [3]. Coffignier (1924) gives *bleu céleste*, celestial blue, as the common French term for cœruleum, the pigment now called [[cerulean]] [3]. So in a nineteenth-century catalog the name could mean either a reduced iron blue or a cobalt-tin sky blue, depending on the maker and language.

sections.title: The swatch and the word list
sections.body: Paterson defines the color simply as a greenish blue [4]. The swatch here comes from Maerz & Paul's dictionary, which gives first use as 1535, plate 35 D 3, and files it under fashion and textiles [5]. It is nearly a grey, with chroma 8, so the page shows a tinted grey, not a saturated sky [5]. The Maerz & Paul entry is a different lineage from the paint: the library also lists Celestial Blue as an alternate name for Cadet Grey [5]. Books disagree, then, on whether *celestial blue* means a greenish blue, a grey, or a reduced Prussian blue [1][4][5].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The library reads the swatch at lightness 60, chroma 8 and hue 218 in LCH; its nearest named color is a plain grey, 7.7 apart in ΔE, with [[cadet-blue]] and [[sky-blue]] as the nearest blue names [5]. Screen colors are approximate.
